NodePoolUpdate is the schema for cluster nodepool replacement definitions in Wayfinder

<a id="nestedblock--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec`

Required:

- `options` (Block List, Min: 1, Max: 1) Options are the options for the update or replacement strategy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--options))

Optional:

- `awaiting_approval` (Boolean)
- `new_spec` (Block List, Max: 1) NewSpec is the desired spec of the existing (if updated) or new node pool (if replaced) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec))
- `next_steps` (Block List, Max: 1) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--next_steps))
- `node_pool_to_update` (String) NodePoolToUpdate is the reference to the NodePool metadata.Name to be updated / replaced
- `pre_requisite` (Block List, Max: 1) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--pre_requisite))
- `target_kubernetes_version` (String) TargetKubernetesVersion is the specific Kubernetes version to use for the new node pool spec - Only valid when a channel is also specified - Normally be an increment of the current, existing NodePool version - Not be greater than the cluster version

<a id="nestedblock--spec--options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.options`

Optional:

- `cloud_update_strategy` (String) CloudUpdateStrategy is how the cloud provider can update the node pool (if at all)
- `new_replacement_config` (Block List, Max: 1) NewReplacementConfig specifies how to create a new node pool and migrate workloads to it (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--options--new_replacement_config))
- `replacement_strategy` (String) ReplacementStrategy is how node pools can get replaced when required

<a id="nestedblock--spec--options--new_replacement_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.options.new_replacement_config`

Optional:

- `node_drain_time_out` (String) NodeDrainTimeOut is the delay to wait for a node to drain before force deleting it After this delay and then the node will be force deleted



<a id="nestedblock--spec--new_spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.new_spec`

Required:

- `image` (String) Image is the image we should use on the instances of this pool
- `machine` (String) Machine is the instance type of the nodes in the poll
- `size` (Number) Size is initial size if autoscaling defined - or the effective size if no autoscaling is enabled

Optional:

- `autoscaling` (Block List, Max: 1) Autoscaling indicates the node pool should autoscale (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec--autoscaling))
- `channel` (String) Channel describes the channel a NodePool follows If specified on a cluster, must be identical to the channel on the cluster
- `cloud_resource_name` (String) CloudResourceName is the name of the cloud resource - should not be set by the client - set by the NodePool mutate if empty - set by the NodePoolUpdate controller depending on the update type
- `default_update_options` (Block List, Max: 1) DefaultUpdateOptions defines how this nodepool can be upgraded - Used by the cluster controller to generate NodePoolUpdates based on spec changes - Ignored when a NodePoolUpdate is created directly (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec--default_update_options))
- `description` (String) Description provides an optional description to the node pool
- `disk_size` (Number) DiskSize is the amount of disk space to assign to the nodes in MBs
- `expires` (String) Expires provides a time for automatic expiration of the cluster
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels is a collection of label placed on to the nodepool
- `logical_name` (String) LogicalName is the internally unique name of the NodePool (not in cloud) - Should always be consistent with a single name entry in a Cluster or NodePoolUpdate - Has to be unique across all nodepools on the Cluster spec - Will NOT always match the name of the NodePool in cloud - Should be treated as an immutable field
- `max_pods_per_node` (Number) MaxPodsPerNode controls how many pods can be scheduled onto each node in this pool
- `provider_details` (Block List, Max: 1) ProviderDetails provides any cloud specific options for this nodepool (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec--provider_details))
- `spot` (Block List, Max: 1) Spot if defines enables nodepool to use spot instances (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec--spot))
- `taints` (Block List) Taints defines a collection scheduling taints placed on the nodepool (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--new_spec--taints))
- `version` (String) Version is the specified version of kubernetes on the node pool This cannot be set by a client if a channel is also specified Will be set by the NodePoolUpdate controller on actual nodepools if a channel is specified
- `zones` (List of String) Zones defines a list of cloud specific availability zones where the nodes are permitted to run

<a id="nestedblock--spec--new_spec--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.new_spec.autoscaling`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enabled indicates the node pool to use autoscaling
- `max_size` (Number) MaxSize is the maximum number of nodes if autoscaling is enabled
- `min_size` (Number) MinSize is minimum number of nodes if autoscaling is enabled

- `replacement_strategy` (String) ReplacementStrategy is how node pools can get replaced when required

### Nested Schema for `spec.new_spec.provider_details.aks`

Optional:

- `mode` (String) Mode is the type of the node pool. System node pools serve the primary purpose of hosting critical system pods such as CoreDNS and tunnelfront. User node pools serve the primary purpose of hosting your application pods.


<a id="nestedblock--spec--new_spec--provider_details--eks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.new_spec.provider_details.eks`

Optional:

- `ami` (String) AMI is a custom image we should use for this nodepool
- `e_c_2_ssh_key` (String) EC2SSHKey is the Amazon EC2 SSH key that provides access for SSH communication with the worker nodes in the managed node group https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-key-pairs.html
- `ssh_source_security_groups` (List of String) SSHSourceSecurityGroups is the security groups that are allowed SSH access (port 22) to the worker nodes
- `user_data` (String) UserData for the launch configuration

### Nested Schema for `spec.new_spec.provider_details.gke`

Optional:

- `enable_autoupgrade` (Boolean) EnableAutoUpgrade indicates if the node group should be configured with auto-upgrading enabled. This must be true if the cluster has ReleaseChannel set.
